title: Dominic and the Choir
premise: Theo Blackwood has spent her life stealing memories for the smuggler guilds of Thornfell, keeping her own past locked away where no one can touch it. When she discovers her face in a century-old book of prophecies—foretold as the one who will either free or destroy King Aldric, whose body has been slowly consumed by a crown-bound entity called the Regent—she becomes hunted by both the guilds and the crown. Forced into an uneasy alliance with the Choir, a hidden order of memory-singers who once tried to save Aldric, Theo learns that the Regent feeds on forgotten things, and that her own stolen-away childhood is the key to unbinding him. In the end, Theo must surrender her most precious memories to the moon's thirteenth turn, trading her invisibility for belonging: she frees Aldric, dismantles the Regent, and finds in the Choir the family she never let herself want.
about_author: Mara Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters nobody ever claimed, which is where she learned that memory is the truest form of treasure. She writes fantasy about outsiders finding their people from a drafty house at the edge of the mountains.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Theo Blackwood lifts a merchant's first kiss from his mind on a rain-slicked night in Thornfell's lower city, then sells it to a grieving widow. POV: Theo. The beat establishes her cold competence and the hollow ritual of her trade—she takes memories but keeps none of her own.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Dust
chapters.summary: Hiding in the archive of a burned library after a job goes wrong, Theo finds a prophecy book from a century ago bearing tomorrow's date—and her own face sketched beside a crowned figure. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a life built on invisibility suddenly having a written destiny.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Theo's handler, Vess, learns of the prophecy and offers to sell Theo to the crown's inquisitors—for Theo's own protection, she claims. POV: Theo. Beat: betrayal by the only structure she trusted, forcing her to flee into the mountains with nothing but the stolen book.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Pursued through the Thornfell passes, Theo realizes the mountain paths themselves are shifting around her, guided by something that knows the prophecy too. POV: Theo. Beat: paranoia deepening into dread as the landscape seems to conspire toward a destination not her own.

chapters.title: Voices Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Trapped in a frozen gorge, Theo hears harmonized singing rising from beneath the ice and follows it to a concealed door. She is captured by the Choir—memory-singers in grey robes—who recognize her on sight. POV: Theo. Beat: terror giving way to reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: Choir leader Sera Vane explains the prophecy: the Regent, a parasitic entity bound into King Aldric's crown, feeds on forgotten memories and will consume the kingdom when the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Only the foretold thief can enter the king's mind. POV: Sera. Beat: exposition laced with Sera's private guilt over a failed rescue attempt years ago.

chapters.title: Lessons in Losing
chapters.summary: Theo trains with young singer Bram, learning to navigate memories that aren't hers. She is clumsy, defensive, and refuses to sing her own past aloud. POV: Bram. Beat: through an outsider's eyes we see Theo's armor—and the first flicker of warmth between them.

chapters.title: The King Who Waits
chapters.summary: The Choir smuggles Theo toward the capital; en route she touches a relic of Aldric's coronation and glimpses the man he was before the Regent took hold. POV: Theo. Beat: unexpected tenderness for a stranger, and the first hint that freeing him may cost her everything.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Gate
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitors raid the Choir's waystation, led by Vess, who has fully defected. A singer dies covering the others' escape. POV: Sera. Beat: grief and fury; the stakes turn from abstract prophecy to blood.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Twelve Gone
chapters.summary: With one lunar turn remaining, the Choir performs a rite that lets Theo rehearse entering a mind—but the rehearsal tears loose a fragment of Theo's sealed childhood: a burning house, a woman singing. POV: Theo. Beat: the past she guarded begins leaking, and she hates how much she wants more.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: Sera reveals the truth: the Choir can open the king's mind, but the Regent devours whatever memories the intruder values most. Theo accuses them of recruiting a sacrifice. POV: Theo. Beat: rupture of trust; Theo walks out into the snow alone.

chapters.title: Vess's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captured by Vess, Theo learns the inquisitors don't serve the king—they serve the Regent, harvesting forgotten memories to feed it. Vess offers Theo her erased childhood back if she betrays the Choir. POV: Vess. Beat: temptation rendered intimate; Vess genuinely believes she's saving Theo.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Shown a vial containing her own earliest memory, Theo realizes the Regent took her family's memories years ago—and that the burning house was real. She escapes, taking the vial. POV: Theo. Beat: rage transmuted into purpose; the mission becomes personal.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Dark
chapters.summary: Bram finds Theo half-frozen and doesn't lecture, just shares bread and a song. Theo returns to the Choir and apologizes—not for leaving, but for assuming they'd wanted a pawn. POV: Bram. Beat: reconciliation; found family solidifying through small kindnesses rather than speeches.

chapters.title: The Palace of Forgotten Things
chapters.summary: The Choir infiltrates the capital during the Moonturn festival. Inside the palace, Theo sees the Regent's influence everywhere: servants with blank eyes, rooms where no one remembers why they came. POV: Sera. Beat: creeping horror; the enemy is already everywhere.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Theo reaches Aldric, who is lucid for a few precious minutes. He begs her not to save him if the cost is another person's self—and gives her a memory of his own to carry out. POV: Aldric. Beat: tragic nobility; the king asks to be seen, not saved.

chapters.title: Descent into the Crown
chapters.summary: The Choir sings the door open and Theo enters Aldric's mindscape: a palace of his memories, corridors collapsing as the Regent eats outward from the throne room. POV: Theo. Beat: awe and claustrophobia; the climax begins.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Face
chapters.summary: The Regent tempts Theo with the rest of her stolen childhood, revealing it orchestrated the prophecy itself—it needed a thief to deliver fresh memories to its feast. POV: Theo. Beat: the trap snaps shut; all her choices were steered.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: As the moon completes its cycle above, Theo chooses: instead of fighting for her memories, she gives them freely—the vial, her childhood, her name—to the Choir below, who sing them back into the world so the Regent can claim nothing. Starved mid-feast, it unravels. POV: Theo. Beat: climactic sacrifice through generosity rather than violence.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Theo wakes emptied but alive; Aldric, freed, begins restoring what he can from the memories she carried out—including fragments of her mother's song. POV: Aldric. Beat: quiet devastation and grace; some losses are permanent, and the story doesn't pretend otherwise.

chapters.title: The Choir Takes a New Voice
chapters.summary: Aldric reforms the court with the Choir as keepers of memory; Vess, broken by the Regent's fall, turns herself in. Theo, memory-poor but surrounded by people who remember for her, is asked to stay. POV: Sera. Beat: the world rebuilding; belonging offered without condition.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Choir
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo—renamed Dominic after the name her mother sang—trains new singers under Thornfell's moon. She still steals the occasional memory, but now she always gives them back. POV: Dominic. Beat: resolution; the invisible girl becomes someone remembered, and remembers herself at last.
